exemplars.title: Disclose with Care: AI Scaffolds for Privacy in Chatbot Interviews
exemplars.why: The evidence directly identifies both defining regions: scrollable user–chatbot logs and a composition area containing a text box and send affordance.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Selected above rid 3645 because it explicitly establishes scrollability in addition to the transcript, input, and send control.

exemplars.title: Chatbots for Data Collection in Surveys: A Comparison of Four Theory-Based Interview Probes
exemplars.why: Its message-bubble list plus bottom input area and submit button provides an unusually direct, reconstruction-ready description of the two-region layout.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Selected above rid 8454 because both the message list and composition controls are explicit, whereas rid 8454 leaves the transcript structure implicit.

exemplars.title: Meta-evaluating the Effects of Social Preferences on NPC-evaluators in an Energy Community Game
exemplars.why: The main surface is explicitly a chat interface, and free-form replies are entered through a box anchored at the bottom, substantially supporting the two-region structure.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Selected above rid 10412 because it identifies the chat surface and bottom composer together, while rid 10412 documents only the attributed-history region.

notes: I reversed the two consensus-tied leaders: rid 9215 is first because its evidence explicitly states that the log is scrollable, completing more of the structural signature. Otherwise, the consensus ordering is retained, with no score adjustment larger than 0.3. Readers should distrust any implication that these ordinary panels were the papers’ novel or impactful contributions. The evidence for rid 8454 is also materially weaker than for the first two: scrolling, persistent history, append behavior, and speaker attribution are inferred from “chat interface” rather than directly documented.
